lesson.grammar_point: integrated review of modal perfects, wish, reported speech and hedging
phases: The Words of the Working Session

listenings.text: An hour in which four people tell each other what they already know is not a session. It is a newsletter that costs four salaries. So I build the agenda backwards. I start from the decisions, one line each, and after every line I ask the same question. Who has to be in the room for that decision to be legal, and does anybody else need to be there at all. Usually the answer removes two people, and the two who leave are relieved. Then I hold the clock, and I hold it even when the conversation is good. Especially when it is good, in fact, because a good conversation is the most expensive way there is to avoid a decision. And in the last five minutes I read back what was closed, with a name and a date against every line, out loud. If nobody objects, it happened. If somebody objects, better now than in three weeks.

Two functions almost never disagree about a number. They disagree about which question the number answers, and then they argue for an hour as though it were arithmetic. So the first thing I do, in front of everybody and before anyone starts defending anything, is reconcile the two versions. Their figure. My figure. The gap. And exactly what the gap is made of. Nine times out of ten the gap is one assumption, and it is never the one anybody expected walking in. Once that assumption has a name on the screen, landing on a single number takes about four minutes, and the hour we were going to spend on it disappears. The other habit I hold on to is closing the loop. A loop that nobody closes does not stay open politely. It closes by itself, in the worst possible way, and you find out about it from somebody else.

extra_audio.text: We should have flagged the capacity gap in April, and the handover was never written down. I wish we had sequenced it the other way round: capacity confirmed, then pricing agreed. Mexico asked me when the handover would be signed, and I told them the fifteenth. Next quarter is likely to land between eleven and thirteen, and I will firm it up after the dry run.
